lessons.title: The merger and the first Super Bowl
lessons.objective: You can explain the AFC/NFC split.

payload.prompt: Put the AFL-NFL merger timeline in order.

items.text: The AFL (American Football League) is founded as a rival to the NFL.
items.why: The AFL started in 1960 to compete with the established NFL.

items.text: The AFL and NFL agree to merge.
items.why: In 1966, the two leagues announced they would combine, ending the rivalry.

items.text: The first Super Bowl: NFL champion Packers beat AFL champion Chiefs.
items.why: Super Bowl I was played in January 1967, between the two league champions, while the leagues were still separate.

items.text: The merger is fully complete; the AFL is officially gone.
items.why: By 1970, the leagues had fully combined into one 26-team NFL.

explanation.correct: The merger took years: rivalry from 1960, agreement in 1966, Super Bowl I in January 1967, one league by 1970.
explanation.incorrect: The merger was a process, not a single year. The AFL started in 1960, the leagues agreed to merge in 1966, and the first Super Bowl was played in January 1967.

payload.prompt: Why did the AFL-NFL merger create the Super Bowl?

options.text: The merger agreement set up a title game between the two leagues' champions.
The NFL wanted to eliminate the AFL as a competitor.
Fans voted on which two teams should play.

explanation.correct: The Super Bowl began as the championship game between the AFL and NFL champions, part of the deal that let the two leagues combine.
explanation.incorrect: The merger agreement is what created the Super Bowl: a showcase game between the champions of the two leagues.

statement.speaker: Fan
statement.text: The AFC used to be the AFL. That is wild. So the Seahawks are in the NFC, which is the old NFL?

payload.question: What is the fan saying?

options.text: The AFC is built on the old AFL and the NFC on the old NFL, mostly.
The Seahawks have never been in the NFC
The AFC is older than the NFC
The merger created brand new conferences with no history

payload.translation: When the leagues fully merged, the old AFL teams formed the AFC and most of the old NFL teams formed the NFC. Three old NFL teams (Browns, Steelers, Colts) moved to the AFC to even things out. The Seahawks have been in the NFC since 2002, after starting in the AFC.

followUps.line: Which teams were original AFL teams?
followUps.why: Names like the Chiefs, Raiders, Jets, Bills, Broncos and Patriots started in the AFL.

followUps.line: Why are the Steelers and Browns in the AFC?
followUps.why: Three old NFL teams moved over so each conference had the same number of teams.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If unsure: AFC is mostly the old AFL, NFC is mostly the old NFL. Ask which teams moved.

payload.prompt: Before the merger, only the NFL existed. True or false?

scene.alt: The AFL and NFL existing as separate rival leagues in the 1960s.

explanation.correct: False. The AFL was founded in 1960 as a rival league, and it competed with the NFL for a decade before they merged.
explanation.incorrect: Yes, the AFL was a separate league for 10 years. The merger combined them into what we know today.

payload.prompt: What year did the NFL-AFL merger agreement happen?

explanation.correct: The merger was announced in 1966. The leagues agreed to combine, with full integration happening by 1970.
explanation.incorrect: The AFL-NFL merger agreement was 1966. The AFL had been around since 1960, and it took time to negotiate the deal.

lessons.title: Dynasties
lessons.objective: You can name what makes a dynasty.

payload.prompt: What makes a team a dynasty?

options.text: Winning multiple championships (Super Bowls) over several years with a core group of players and coaches.
Winning just one Super Bowl and never losing again.
Having the same team logo and colors forever.

explanation.correct: A dynasty is sustained excellence: several championships over a stretch of years, usually with a core of players and a consistent coach. Think Steelers of the 1970s, Cowboys of the 1990s, Patriots of the 2000s and 2010s.
explanation.incorrect: A dynasty is not a one-hit wonder. It is long-term dominance with multiple Super Bowl wins.

statement.speaker: Analyst
statement.text: The 1970s Steelers won four Super Bowls in six years. That is the gold standard dynasty.

payload.question: What is the analyst saying?

options.text: The Steelers never won another game after 1979.
Winning multiple titles in a short window defines a dynasty and sets the bar for greatness.
The Steelers only won one Super Bowl.
The Steelers are the only dynasty ever.

payload.translation: The 1970s Steelers are the template for what a dynasty looks like: consistent, dominant, multiple championships. Four Super Bowls in six years is extraordinary.

followUps.line: How many Super Bowls did the Patriots win in their run?
followUps.why: Six, across the 2001 to 2018 seasons. It is the modern dynasty fans compare to everything else.
Stars age, salary-cap pressure builds and coaches move on. Eventually even the best teams reset.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If unsure, think about teams that won a lot of titles close together over years.

payload.prompt: Match each dynasty to its era.

pairs.definition: Won four Super Bowls (1974, 1975, 1978 and 1979 seasons) behind the Steel Curtain defense.
Won three Super Bowls in four seasons (1992, 1993 and 1995) with a star-studded offense.
Won six Super Bowls between the 2001 and 2018 seasons, the dominant dynasty of the salary-cap era.

explanation.summary: Each dynasty had its own style: a great defense, a star-powered offense, and sustained excellence through the salary-cap era.
explanation.sayThisLine: Steelers were the Steel Curtain. Cowboys were star-powered. Patriots stayed great the longest.

payload.prompt: A dynasty just won its fourth Super Bowl in six years. Can it stay on top?

facts.label: Recent wins
facts.value: Four Super Bowls in six years

facts.label: Draft picks
facts.value: Used on trades and free agency, not rebuilding

facts.label: Salary cap
facts.value: Tight; hard to bring in young talent

options.label: Rebuild while you can
options.consequence: Dynasties eventually end. Age and cap pressure force a reset. Starting early lets you stay competitive instead of falling off a cliff.

options.label: Go all-in one more year
options.consequence: You might win another title. But if you fail, you are stuck with old, expensive players and a weak draft class.
considerations: One more shot can feel worth it.

payload.expertNote: Every dynasty ends. The smartest teams refresh the roster before the decline, not after, because aging stars and cap pressure catch up quickly.

lessons.title: Plays everyone quotes
lessons.objective: You can recognize the famous plays.

payload.prompt: Match each famous play to what happened.

pairs.definition: Steelers-Raiders playoff: Franco Harris caught a deflected pass and scored the winner.
49ers-Cowboys NFC title game: Dwight Clark leaped for Joe Montana's pass in the end zone.
Super Bowl XLII: David Tyree pinned a pass to his helmet as the Giants upset the Patriots.

distractorDefinitions: A quarterback ran in untouched for a 99-yard touchdown.
A running back threw a pass that was caught by the kicker.

explanation.summary: These plays are quoted forever because they were dramatic, came in huge games and looked almost impossible.
explanation.sayThisLine: Immaculate was a bounce. The Catch was a leap. The Helmet Catch was a pin.

statement.speaker: Broadcaster
statement.text: Hail Mary! The quarterback heaves it into a crowded end zone and everyone hopes for a bounce.

payload.question: What is the broadcaster saying?

options.text: A Hail Mary is a planned play with smart reads and progressions.
A Hail Mary is a desperate long throw into a crowded end zone, usually as time expires, with low odds of working.
A Hail Mary is a running play.
A Hail Mary is called every time the quarterback throws deep.

payload.translation: A Hail Mary is a desperation long throw into a crowd in the end zone, usually as time expires. It is low odds: a tip, a scramble or a jump ball decides it.

followUps.line: Why is it called a Hail Mary?
followUps.why: Because the throw is a prayer. Hail Mary is a Catholic prayer, and the nickname stuck after a famous playoff throw in the 1970s.
On the last play of a half or game when there is no time for anything else.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Call it a prayer with low odds, not a real strategy. It is what you do when time is running out.

payload.prompt: Why do fans quote famous plays decades later?

options.text: They were clutch moments in big games that looked impossible and are still hard to believe.
Because the quarterback threw a interception and it was funny.
Because it was the highest-scoring game ever.

explanation.correct: The plays fans quote are the ones that looked impossible in huge games: The Catch, the Immaculate Reception, the Helmet Catch. That is lore.
explanation.incorrect: Lore lives because moments were shocking and high-stakes. Routine plays are forgotten.

payload.prompt: The Immaculate Reception, The Catch and the Helmet Catch all happened in playoff games. True or false?

scene.alt: Three famous plays, each from a playoff or championship game.

explanation.correct: True. The Immaculate Reception was a playoff game, The Catch was the NFC Championship and the Helmet Catch was in the Super Bowl. High stakes help make lore.
explanation.incorrect: All three came in playoff games, which is part of why they are remembered.

lessons.title: The Hall of Fame
lessons.objective: You can explain Canton and the yearly debate.

payload.prompt: What is the Pro Football Hall of Fame?

options.text: A museum in Canton, Ohio where the greatest players, coaches and contributors are honored with a plaque and enshrinement ceremony.
A list the NFL keeps to track statistics.
A fantasy football league for old players.

explanation.correct: Canton is the Hall. Enshrinees get a bronze bust and a speech at an annual ceremony each August. It is the highest honor in the sport.
explanation.incorrect: The Hall of Fame is sacred in football culture, in Canton, Ohio, with enshrinement in August.

statement.speaker: Fan
statement.text: Every year around the Super Bowl, the Hall of Fame voting is a huge argument. Deserving guys get left out.

payload.question: What is the fan saying?

options.text: The Hall voting is objective and nobody ever disagrees.
The Hall selection process is subjective and voters sometimes pass on guys who fans think belong.
The Hall only votes once every 10 years.
Players vote themselves into the Hall.

payload.translation: Every year, the Hall voting creates debate: 'He should have been in!' and 'That guy? Really?'. It is one of the biggest arguments in football.

followUps.why: A committee of selectors, not fans. They can disagree on borderline cases.

followUps.line: What if you disagree with the voting?
followUps.why: Fans debate it forever. Some great players wait years. That argument is part of the fun.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If unsure, remember: the Hall is debated every year. No one agrees 100%.

payload.prompt: Match the honor to the description.

pairs.definition: Being formally inducted: a bronze bust in Canton and a speech.
A player voted in the first year he is eligible, five years after retiring.
The yearly argument over who got in and who got snubbed.

explanation.summary: Enshrinement is the honor. First ballot is the elite path. The yearly debate is guaranteed.
explanation.sayThisLine: Enshrined means he made it. First ballot means it was obvious. Debate means somebody got snubbed.

payload.prompt: What year did the Pro Football Hall of Fame open in Canton, Ohio?

explanation.correct: The Pro Football Hall of Fame opened in Canton in 1963. It is the official home of the game's greatest.
explanation.incorrect: Canton became the Hall of Fame's home in 1963. It is now a pilgrimage site for football fans.

lessons.title: Thanksgiving and traditions
lessons.objective: You can say why football owns holidays.

statement.speaker: Grandma
statement.text: Thanksgiving football is as much a tradition to me as the turkey.

payload.question: What is she saying?

options.text: Football games are not part of holiday celebrations.
For many families, watching football on certain holidays (like Thanksgiving) is now a core holiday tradition.
Football only happens in the off-season.
The Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys do not play on Thanksgiving.

payload.translation: Football on Thanksgiving, with the Lions and Cowboys hosting games, has become a family ritual for many households, like Super Bowl Sunday.

followUps.line: Which teams play on Thanksgiving every year?
followUps.why: The Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys host games on Thanksgiving, a long-standing tradition, plus another game.

followUps.line: Why is Super Bowl Sunday like a holiday?
followUps.why: Parties, food, ads and the halftime show. Even people who do not follow football tune in.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If unsure, think about your own family's holiday traditions. Many include a football game now.

payload.title: Game day traditions
payload.setting: Planning an outing with someone who loves game day culture.

exchanges.theirMessage: You have to come to a game with me. The tailgate is half the fun, and then we watch our team beat the rival.

replies.text: I am in. What do I bring to the tailgate?
replies.theirResponse: Yes! Just bring drinks or snacks. The parking lot gets loud and everyone is together.
replies.coachNote: Shows you know tailgating is a pre-game party and you are ready to join.

replies.text: Maybe. What time do you usually go?
replies.theirResponse: Hours before kickoff. People show up early for tailgating.
replies.coachNote: Reasonable question, but more enthusiasm would help.

replies.text: I will just come for the game itself.
replies.theirResponse: You are missing the best part though.
replies.coachNote: Tailgating is the tradition they love. Skipping it misses their favorite part.

payload.closingNote: Game day for true fans starts in the parking lot hours early. That is the ritual they love.

payload.prompt: Why are division rivalry games bigger than regular-season games?

options.text: Deep history, repeat matchups twice a year, and fans who grew up with the beef between teams make them intense.
Because the rules are different in rivalry games.
Because the Super Bowl is only between division rivals.

explanation.correct: Rivalries are built on history, geography and fan bases that have shared decades of big games. Play twice a year for 50 years and it becomes lore.
explanation.incorrect: Rivalry games matter because of tradition and history, not different rules. Records matter less when the stakes are pride.

payload.prompt: Super Bowl Sunday is an unofficial American holiday. True or false?

scene.alt: Millions of people watching the Super Bowl together as a cultural event.

explanation.correct: True. While not a national holiday off work, Super Bowl Sunday is treated like one. Parties, ads, halftime show, food. Millions of people celebrate it.
explanation.incorrect: Yes, Super Bowl Sunday is a cultural event so big that many people treat it like a real holiday, even if it is not officially one.
